description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of five different model configurations—Single-task_baseline, Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout, Unsupervised_SimCSE, Supervised_SimCSE, and 2-Tier SimCSE—across three evaluation metrics: Sentiment Accuracy (light brown), STS Correlation (maroon), and Paraphrase Accuracy (teal), as reported in the paper “2-Tier SimCSE: Elevating BERT for Robust Sentence Embeddings.” The vertical axis represents “Accuracy / Correlation” on a linear scale from 0 to 0.8, with major tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Each model configuration is represented by a group of three adjacent bars, with the legend indicating color coding. For Sentiment Accuracy, performance ranges from approximately 0.48 to 0.53, with the Single-task_baseline achieving the highest value (~0.53) and Supervised_SimCSE the lowest (~0.48). STS Correlation shows a clear upward trend across the models, starting at ~0.50 for Single-task_baseline and reaching ~0.81 for both Supervised_SimCSE and 2-Tier SimCSE, indicating strong semantic similarity performance. Paraphrase Accuracy remains relatively stable across all models, ranging from ~0.78 to ~0.80, with Single-task_baseline and Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout slightly higher (~0.80) than the others (~0.78–0.79). The 2-Tier SimCSE model matches Supervised_SimCSE in STS Correlation and slightly underperforms in Sentiment Accuracy, while maintaining high Paraphrase Accuracy, suggesting its robustness across diverse sentence embedding tasks.
